source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A condition generally considered unrelated to how bilirubin is actually metabolized and processed by the body","B":"A biliary obstruction problem, rather than the pre-hepatic process this particular lab pattern actually points toward","C":"A pre-hepatic cause, such as increased red blood cell breakdown (hemolysis), rather than a liver or biliary excretion problem","D":"A fairly ordinary, normal finding that would not typically call for any further clinical evaluation"}}
source_row.rationale: Elevated indirect (unconjugated) bilirubin with normal direct (conjugated) bilirubin is more suggestive of a pre-hepatic cause, such as increased red blood cell breakdown (hemolysis), since this pattern reflects increased bilirubin production before the liver has had the opportunity to conjugate it, rather than a liver or biliary excretion problem.
